# s232 — File open GitHub issues as roadmap rows

`slicer issues-pull` turns a project's open GitHub issues into unscored roadmap rows, one per issue, keyed so a rerun never files the same issue twice.

**Findings:** follow-up to s231: issues filed on GitHub have to be retyped as roadmap rows · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-07** — Ready for review: slicer issues-pull added (github.py second exact gh form + list_open_issues; ops.pull_issues; cli.cmd_issues_pull fetches unlocked then writes under project_lock via _mutating). tests/test_issues_pull.py (19 tests) plus allowlist and ai split cases; full suite 1483 OK (1 skipped). Docs, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG updated. Config: issues_repo=squalor-xyz/slicer and version bumped 1->5 on owner's instruction. Dry run against squalor-xyz/slicer: zero open issues. Deviation: created is [] under --dry-run (items carries the would-file rows with id null).

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** filing issues back to GitHub, refreshing a title after the first pull, closing or retiring a row when the issue closes, mapping labels to statuses or scores, importing bodies or comments, paging past one gh response, a --state flag, a TUI action, or auto-promote.

## Why

Issues filed against a project's repository should become roadmap rows without someone retyping them. s231 sends local feedback out as issues; this is the way back in. The command is for any project. This repo is only a configured user of it: `issues_repo` in this project's config is `squalor-xyz/slicer`, and that string does not appear as a constant in `src/slicer/`.

An issue body is untrusted. It becomes a URL on an open row, not a slice an agent would follow. Rows land unscored and with no pass, so triage stays with the owner.

## Failing tests

- `--dry-run` calls `gh issue list` once, writes nothing (index, log, slices, render, and `.slicer/lock` contents unchanged), and returns what it would file and reuse.
- The first pull files one open row per issue with no slice: filing key `github:OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`, findings equal to the issue URL, importance 2, urgency 2, effort unset, and an empty pass. Rows are appended in ascending issue number.
- The argv is exactly `gh issue list --repo OWNER/REPO --state open --limit N --json number,title,url`. It never asks for `body`. The fake returns a body field anyway, and no body text appears in the index, a slice, the log, or render output.
- A second pull reuses existing items by key and does not change their title, status, findings, scores, or pass, even when the GitHub title changed. When every issue already has a key, nothing is written, `--render` renders nothing, and the exit is 0.
- A row keyed to an issue that is now retired or done is reused, not refiled.
- Preflight is all-or-nothing. A blank title, a number that is not a positive integer, a URL that is not `https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/issues/NUMBER` for the requested repo and that number, or a duplicate number in one response refuses the whole pull. The error names the issue number and keeps `add`'s code (`blank_title`, otherwise `external`). Nothing is written.
- A missing `gh`, a nonzero `gh`, output that is not JSON, or JSON that is not a list of `{number, title, url}` objects is code `external` (exit 2). Nothing is written and `issue create` is never run.
- `--limit` defaults to 30. A value below 1 or above 100 is `usage` before `gh` runs. The command follows no further pages.
- Repo resolution matches `feedback-report`: `--repo`, else a nonempty `issues_repo`, else `usage` with nothing contacted. A malformed `--repo` is `usage`.
- The project lock is not held while `gh` runs. A fake `gh` that tries to take the lock with a zero timeout succeeds.
- A merge in progress refuses the write (`merge_in_progress`) after the fetch. The dry run is still allowed.
- `--render` renders after the write. `--strict` with a failing render leaves the previous index, log, and render on disk. `--strict` without `--render` is `usage`, as with other mutations.
- Unscored new open rows get the same stderr hint `add` prints, once per run, naming every new id.
- JSON is `{repo, dry_run, created, reused, items}`. Both lists stay present under `--lean`.

## Implement

`slicer issues-pull` is a roadmap write. It reuses s231's `gh` runner and `issues_repo` resolution.

`main` holds the project lock for a whole handler marked `mutates`. Do not mark this one, or the lock is held across the network call. Fetch first with no lock, the way `next --start` takes its own lock in `cmd_next`. Validate and preflight every issue against the current state, with the same title rules as `add` (`ops._reject_bad_text`). Then take `store.project_lock`, call `vcs.require_no_merge`, reload state, recompute which keys already exist (another writer may have filed some), and add the rest through `ops`. `--render` and `--strict` behave as they do for `add`. Route the locked write through the same render-after and render-first helpers `_mutating` uses, rather than a second copy of them.

`--dry-run` still calls `gh`, because that call is a read. It writes nothing and takes no lock. The real command writes. It takes no `--yes`; creating issues is the other command.

The only list invocation is:

```sh
gh issue list --repo OWNER/REPO --state open --limit N --json number,title,url
```

`--limit` defaults to 30 and the maximum is 100, so one run cannot flood the queue. Above 100 or below 1 is `usage`, not a silent clamp. State stays open. There is no `--state` flag in this slice.

Each new row is an open item with no slice. The filing key is `github:OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`, using the validated repo string with no case folding. Findings is the issue URL, one line. The pass is empty: pass `pass_key=""` explicitly, because an omitted pass inherits the previous item's. The body is never requested or stored. Strip the title and keep it otherwise as GitHub has it; a title containing a newline fails the preflight with `newline_in_field`.

A key that already exists returns that item in any status, including when the GitHub title differs. This slice does not refresh titles. An all-existing pull writes nothing and does not render. Labels do not become statuses.

JSON is `{repo, dry_run, created, reused, items}`. `created` and `reused` are id lists. Each item has `number`, `title` (as stored), `key`, `id`, and `existing`. Under `--dry-run`, a new row's `id` is null. Text names the ids filed and the ids reused, or says that nothing was new.

This slice does not file issues back to GitHub, close or retire a row when the issue closes, import comments, page past one `gh` response, or promote the new rows.

Put new command lines in fenced blocks in this slice, for the same reason as the report slice.
